source: FICTIONAL desktop-PC maintenance simulation. Illustrative only - not real maintenance advice. Hardware facts to be validated against an equipment source before the main study.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU rocker switch at the rear of the case to O (off).
steps.explanation: The switch isolates mains power from the motherboard. A graphics card must never be handled while the board carries standby voltage.

steps.instruction: Remove the thumbscrew at the top-right corner of the side panel.
steps.explanation: The thumbscrew is the only fastener holding the panel. Loosening it by hand avoids tools scratching the paint.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel off to open the case.
steps.explanation: The panel rides on slots along the case edge. Sliding it back first, then lifting, avoids bending the sheet metal.

steps.instruction: Touch the bare metal of the case to discharge static.
steps.explanation: A graphics card is dense with static-sensitive circuitry. Grounding yourself first protects it even though no spark is visible.

steps.instruction: Unplug the 6-pin PCIe power cable from the top edge of the card.
steps.explanation: The cable feeds the card up to 150 watts. Pulling the connector body, not the wires, keeps the pins from bending.

steps.instruction: Push the retention tab at the far end of the PCIe slot down to release the card.
steps.explanation: The tab is a plastic latch at the slot end. Pressing it unlocks the card's edge connector so the card can lift out.

steps.instruction: Pull the old graphics card straight out of the slot.
steps.explanation: Straight, even pull keeps the edge connector aligned. Tilting the card while it is half-seated can crack the slot.

steps.instruction: Seat the new card firmly into the PCIe slot until the tab clicks.
steps.explanation: The tab clicking means the edge connector is fully home. A half-seated card is the most common cause of no-display faults.

steps.instruction: Plug the 6-pin PCIe power cable back into the top edge of the card.
steps.explanation: The card will not start without auxiliary power. The connector is keyed so it only fits one way round.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel back on until it clicks home.
steps.explanation: Closing the case before power is restored keeps dust out and the airflow path intact.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU power switch back to I (on).
steps.explanation: Power is restored only after every part is secured, so the card powers up in a fully assembled machine.

hazard.message: STATIC WARNING: charge detected on your wrist. Discharge on the case metal before touching the card!
